Customer.title: Customer
Customer.description: Represents a customer who uses the garage services.

id.description: Unique identifier for the customer entity.

Vehicle.title: Vehicle
Vehicle.description: Represents a vehicle owned by a customer.

id.description: Unique identifier for the vehicle entity.

licensePlate.description: License plate number of the vehicle.

Appointment.title: Appointment
Appointment.description: Represents a scheduled appointment for a vehicle.

id.description: Unique identifier for the appointment entity.

status.description: Status of the appointment (e.g., Scheduled, In Progress, QC, Done).

Admin.title: Admin
Admin.description: Represents an admin member of the garage.

id.description: Unique identifier for the admin entity.

firstName.description: First name of the admin member.

lastName.description: Last name of the admin member.

email.description: Email address of the admin member.

phone.description: Phone number of the admin member.

role.description: Role of the admin member (e.g., Mechanic, Service Advisor).

Part.title: Part
Part.description: Represents a part in the inventory.

id.description: Unique identifier for the part entity.

quantity.description: Quantity of the part in stock.

lowStockThreshold.description: The threshold at which stock is considered low.

Service.title: Service
Service.description: Represents a service offered by the garage.

id.description: Unique identifier for the service entity.

Invoice.title: Invoice
Invoice.description: Represents an invoice for services rendered.

id.description: Unique identifier for the invoice entity.

status.description: Status of the invoice (e.g., Issued, Paid, Overdue).

InvoiceItem.title: InvoiceItem
InvoiceItem.description: Represents an item on an invoice, either a part or a service.

id.description: Unique identifier for the invoice item entity.

partId.description: Reference to Part. (Relationship: Part 1:N InvoiceItem).  Null if it is a service.

serviceId.description: Reference to Service. (Relationship: Service 1:N InvoiceItem). Null if it is a part.

quantity.description: Quantity of the part or service.

unitPrice.description: Price per unit of the part or service.

DiagnosticReport.title: DiagnosticReport
DiagnosticReport.description: Represents a diagnostic report generated by the AI.

id.description: Unique identifier for the diagnostic report entity.

description.description: The description of the diagnostic report.

ChatMessage.title: ChatMessage
ChatMessage.description: Represents a chat message between the garage and a customer.

id.description: Unique identifier for the chat message.

customerId.description: Reference to the Customer. (Relationship: Customer 1:N ChatMessage)

adminId.description: Reference to the Admin member. (Relationship: Admin 1:N ChatMessage). Can be null if sent by customer

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to mirror the relationships between entities in the GaragePilot application, while prioritizing security, scalability, and debuggability. It leverages path-based ownership and denormalization to ensure authorization independence, enabling secure and atomic operations. The structure separates data with different access requirements into distinct collections to maintain a homogeneous security posture.  

Authorization Independence is achieved through denormalization. For instance, `customerId` is present on `Vehicle`, `Appointment`, and `Invoice` collections, enabling rules to validate ownership without `get()` calls. Admin roles are managed via a dedicated collection (`/roles_admins/{uid}`) which facilitates simple existence checks in rules.

The QAPs are addressed as follows:
*   **List operations:** Segregation allows for secure list operations. For example, listing all vehicles owned by a customer is achieved via the `/customers/{customerId}/vehicles` collection.
*   **Private data:** Path-based ownership is used for user-specific data like vehicles and appointments ensuring only the customer and authorized admins can access it.
*   **Collaborative data:** Not applicable as there is no collaborative data in the models, though admin access could be modelled using the Membership Map pattern if required in future iterations.

This structure promotes clarity, predictability, and maintainability, aligning with the core design principles.
